concepts.title: Nature and Scope of Human Geography
concepts.definition: Human geography studies the changing relationship between the resting human community and the active physical environment, synthesising ideas from sister disciplines; it moves from nature-humans to humans-nature and finally to human beings as modifiers of the earth.
concepts.key_idea: Geography is the study of areal differentiation: what is where, why there and how it changes through time.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy101.txt nature of human geography and human-environment relationship sections
question_patterns: define human geography and its scope
how does human geography synthesise ideas from other disciplines
what is meant by areal differentiation
trace the shift from nature-humans to humans-nature views
why is human geography called a synthesising discipline
distinguish physical geography from human geography

solution_steps.explain: the interaction of human society with the physical environment is the core object
concepts are borrowed and reworked from sociology, economics, history and biology
explaining why places differ is geography's signature task

concepts.title: Determinism, Possibilism and Neo-determinism
concepts.section: Human Geography Through the Corridors of Time
concepts.definition: Environmental determinism holds that nature controls human life and was associated with Ratzel and Semple; possibilism of Vidal de La Blache and Febvre counters that humans are active agents choosing within limits set by nature; Griffith Taylor's neo-determinism or stop-and-go determinism argues for balanced development respecting both human skill and environmental limits.
concepts.key_idea: The schools differ on agency: nature commands (determinism), humans command (possibilism), or a middle path times human action to environmental tolerance (neo-determinism).
concepts.textbook_ref: legy101.txt determinism, possibilism and neo-determinism passages
question_patterns: compare environmental determinism and possibilism with proponents
who propounded neo-determinism and why is it a middle path
which school did Ratzel and Semple belong to
give an example where possibilism explains human choices
why did scholars reject pure determinism

solution_steps.explain: Ratzel-Semple to determinism; Vidal de La Blache-Febvre to possibilism; Taylor to neo-determinism
air conditioning and greenhouses show humans overcoming nature, the possibilist point
Taylor stops development where environmental tolerance ends and goes where it resumes

concepts.title: Fields and Sub-fields of Human Geography
concepts.section: Fields and Sub-fields of Human Geography
concepts.definition: Human geography branches into social geography, urban and rural geography, population and settlement geography, economic geography (with agriculture, industry and tourism branches), historical, political, bio-geography and environmental geography, each linked to sister disciplines.
concepts.key_idea: Every sub-field pairs a geographical question with the concepts of a sister discipline, which is how the subject keeps expanding.
question_patterns: list the major sub-fields of human geography
which sub-field links geography with political science
define bio-geography as given in the chapter
what is the place of environmental geography among sub-fields

solution_steps.explain: social, urban-rural, population-settlement and economic are the principal fields
each sub-field is born where geography meets a companion discipline
the branches together cover every human activity over space

worked_examples.question_pattern: Contrast environmental determinism and possibilism using one example each.

solution_template.explain: nature dictates livelihood, dress and housing; the equatorial forest tribes illustrate it
technology lets humans farm deserts and build in cold lands, so nature only proposes
modern geography accepts limits but stresses human agency

worked_examples.question_pattern: Explain Griffith Taylor's stop-and-go determinism with its policy meaning.

solution_template.explain: human programmes should fit environmental tolerances rather than fight them
go where nature allows, stop where degradation begins, like traffic lights
it seeks balanced development between fatalism and arrogance

worked_examples.question_pattern: Match four sub-fields of human geography with their sister disciplines.

solution_template.explain: borrows from sociology the study of social groups over space
draws on political science for states, boundaries and power
uses economics for production, exchange and consumption patterns
